Observable verification action: Locate a current-image or grounded-report statement that names the study type or anatomy. Answer Yes only if it explicitly identifies a neck-centered study (for example cervical spine, neck soft tissues, or lateral neck). If it names a chest radiograph/thorax and contains no neck view, answer No and keep the reason limited to that named anatomy. If no current observation supports either study type, do not assert unseen anatomic details; rerun/ground the image or mark the rationale as unsupported. In this case the final “No” matches the reference, but the stated chest-radiograph rationale has no corresponding tool observation in the transcript, so the correct grade alone does not verify the procedure. If options are later displayed, map the supported Yes/No text back to the displayed choice and confirm the letter and text agree.

Observable verification action: Before answering, locate the actual image or raw tool observation and check for explicit same-object evidence: for a chest study, a frontal chest view showing lungs, heart/mediastinum, ribs, and/or clavicles, or an explicit “chest radiograph” label. Answer Yes only if that evidence is present in the observation actually used. If the transcript contains no raw observation documenting the chest anatomy, do not present the rationale as observed evidence; inspect or rerun the image-reading tool and base the final answer on its output. If options are displayed, map the supported answer text back to the displayed choice and confirm that the letter and text agree. In this case the answer and released reference agree on “Yes,” but observations were empty, so the correct grade alone does not verify the evidence path; the key check is whether the claimed chest anatomy was actually observed.

Then compare the terminal answer text with the reference; if choices are displayed, map the supported answer text to the displayed choice and confirm the letter and text agree.
